title: How we taught agents to use good retrieval - Hanna Lichtenberg, Mixedbread AI
talk_summary: Mixedbread argues that reasoning models are bottlenecked by retrieval, not reasoning, and shows better search tools recover much of the oracle gap. They build a search agent with tiered retrieval tools, natural-language query framing, initial semantic preview, deduped parallel searches, and train/evaluate a small model with retrieval and trajectory rewards.

takeaways.technique: Tiered retrieval tools with summaries vs full payload
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose four search tools: overview semantic search returns many chunk summaries, main semantic search returns top full chunks, metadata filter, and grep; the agent picks per query.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent receives up to 50 retrieve chunks. Um and it sees only summaries of the chunk contents

takeaways.what_they_do: Before writing a query, the agent articulates what evidence it needs; for semantic search it is told to write one concise sentence, not a keyword-style search query.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just instructing it to write one concise sentence describing what it wants to find

takeaways.technique: Initial semantic preview plus metadata facets
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent starts with an initial semantic search on the user query and metadata hints, then splits intent into up to four aspects and runs parallel searches within capped rounds.
takeaways.evidence_quote: initially our agent sees the user query, but also already um results from an initial semantic search

takeaways.what_they_do: Tool results are deduplicated before returning to the agent so it never sees the same chunk multiple times.
takeaways.evidence_quote: results of the tools are returned to the agent via deduplicating chunks

takeaways.what_they_do: They train with retrieval reward plus trajectory reward; LLM judges check relevance, whether all chunks are relevant, ranking plausibility, natural query wording, and sufficient exploration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: supervised fine-tuning with a larger teacher LLM. And then we uh did on-policy reinforcement learning with an own search reward
takeaways.numbers: NDCG@10 0.4 vs 0.18; 93.4% accuracy on Snowflake MATCH QA

takeaways.what_they_do: They use a small LLM for the search agent to make it faster and cheaper, training it for tool choice, query quality, exploration, and efficiency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we just decided to have a very small LLM to make the agent even faster
